places.name: Florence Griswold Museum & Artists' Colony
places.summary: The boarding house where American Impressionist painters lived and worked. They painted directly on the doors and wall panels, and those paintings are still there. Outside is the river landscape they painted again and again.
places.why_go: Artists who lived together, ate together and painted on the furniture. It is a real story about people, not just a room full of pictures, and it breaks the drive to the ferry.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's atmospheric interiors and for Stivka's quiet side. The story of the artist community gives everyone something easy to talk about.

hours.note: Sunday hours in the April-December season.

places.address: Florence Griswold Museum, 96 Lyme Street, Old Lyme, Connecticut

places.name: Cross Sound Ferry: New London to Orient Point
places.summary: An 80-minute ferry across Long Island Sound, from New London to Orient Point. You stay on open water the whole way, with lighthouses, small islands and working harbors in view.
places.why_go: The first real moment of the trip, and it saves about six hours of driving around New York City. You are on a boat, not in traffic.
places.best_fit_note: Primary fit: viki, gora. Low physical demand; no skip path is required.

hours.note: Target a late-afternoon vehicle sailing; final October departure grid must be reconfirmed.

places.address: Cross Sound Ferry, 2 Ferry Street, New London, Connecticut

places.skip_strategy: Low physical demand; no skip path is required.

places.name: Greenport Harbor & Mitchell Park Carousel
places.summary: A small harbor village with an antique carousel inside a glass building, looking across at the Shelter Island ferries.
places.why_go: Salt air, boat lights and one silly carousel ride instead of another hotel check-in. A good way to arrive after a long day.
places.best_fit_note: Primary fit: viki, stivka. Low physical demand; no skip path is required.

places.skip_strategy: Low physical demand; no skip path is required.

places.name: The Book Barn
places.summary: A used bookshop that has spread across a whole yard of sheds and gardens, with cats, goats and reading corners between the buildings.
places.why_go: You hunt for books between goats and flower beds. Cheap, warm, and full of small discoveries instead of one polished museum story.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's hidden corners and Stivka's slow browsing. Gora can look for strange history books away from the normal shelves.

places.name: North Ferry to Shelter Island
places.summary: A small working ferry that carries cars across the narrow harbor to Shelter Island. It leaves every few minutes and needs no booking.
places.why_go: Two short ferries make Shelter Island feel like somewhere you found, not somewhere you drove through.
places.best_fit_note: Primary fit: viki, gora. Low physical demand; no skip path is required.

places.summary: A 2,350-acre nature preserve covering almost a third of Shelter Island, with salt marsh, tidal creeks, oak woodland and open meadow. We walk a short loop.
places.why_go: Real quiet nature without a long or hard walk. Water, birds and almost nobody else.

places.name: South Ferry to North Haven

places.why_go: The second short crossing finishes the island loop and means no driving back the way we came.
places.best_fit_note: Primary fit: viki, gora. Low physical demand; no skip path is required.

places.name: Parrish Art Museum
places.summary: A long low museum shaped like two barns, designed by the Swiss architects Herzog & de Meuron, standing in an open meadow. From 25 September 2026 it holds an exhibition on Abstract Expressionism.
places.why_go: A beautiful building full of light, and the story of why so many artists moved out to this coast.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's strong architecture and landscape photos, and for Stivka's thoughtful art talk. Paco gets an easy indoor stop everyone accepts.

hours.note: Thursday-Monday hours.

places.address: Parrish Art Museum, 279 Montauk Highway, Water Mill, New York

places.name: The Big Duck
places.summary: A farm shop from 1931 built in the shape of a giant white duck. Architects still use the word 'duck' for any building shaped like the thing it sells.
places.why_go: Fifteen minutes, one enormous concrete duck, and a real place in architecture history. This is the stop that becomes the group joke.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's strange memory photo, and for Gora, who likes the real story behind a ridiculous object.

hours.note: County lists daily hours but asks visitors to confirm by phone.

places.address: The Big Duck, 1012 Flanders Road, Flanders, New York

places.name: Tanger Outlets Riverhead
places.summary: A large outlet center with Nike, Coach, Armani, Under Armour and dozens of other discount brand shops.
places.why_go: A proper shopping block, planned on purpose so it does not eat into a nature or museum day.
places.best_fit_note: Primary fit: viki. Low physical demand; no skip path is required.

places.name: Long Island Aquarium
places.summary: A small waterfront aquarium with a large living coral reef, a 120,000-gallon shark tank, touch tanks and butterflies.
places.why_go: The safe choice in bad weather, and it also cuts driving on the South Fork. Everyone finds something here.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Paco's wish to keep the group balanced, and for Viki's close-up color photos. The touch tanks keep it social.

hours.note: Open daily except Thanksgiving and Christmas.

places.name: Cradle of Aviation Museum
places.summary: A museum of aircraft built on Long Island, including a real Grumman lunar module. It shows how factories in this suburban corridor helped put people on the Moon.
places.why_go: A real Moon lander, built a few miles away. Serious engineering history, and not another war museum.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Gora's love of engineering and hidden history, and for Viki's photos of spacecraft up close. Stivka gets a hopeful human story.

hours.note: Tuesday-Sunday.

places.address: Cradle of Aviation Museum, Charles Lindbergh Boulevard, Garden City, New York

places.name: Asbury Boardwalk, Convention Hall & Carousel Ruins
places.summary: A seafront of grand old music halls, painted murals, weathered concrete and the roofless shell of an old carousel building.
places.why_go: Beautiful decay next to new paint. The photos are strong, and the story of the town falling apart and coming back is real.
places.best_fit_note: Primary fit: viki, stivka. Low physical demand; no skip path is required.
places.address: Asbury Park Convention Hall, 1300 Ocean Avenue, Asbury Park, New Jersey

places.name: Silverball Retro Arcade
places.summary: Rows of restored pinball and arcade machines, all set to free play after one entry ticket, directly across from the ocean.
places.why_go: Pay once and play everything. Four people can compete, wander off and come back with no planning at all.
places.best_fit_note: Primary fit: gora, sheluvspaco. Low physical demand; no skip path is required.

places.best_fit_note: Good for Stivka's love of rock and metal, and for Gora's social side. Viki gets a whole walkable district instead of one room.

places.name: Ocean Grove Great Auditorium & Tent City
places.summary: A Methodist camp town where canvas tents are still attached to small wooden cottages, laid out in a grid around a wooden auditorium seating 6,250 people. Alcohol is not sold here.
places.why_go: A tent city that has been lived in every summer for 150 years, around a huge wooden hall. Strange, calm, and completely unlike Asbury next door.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Stivka's interest in faith and music, and for Viki's unlikely tent architecture. We visit as guests of a living community.

hours.note: Official landmark walk works in October; interior auditorium tours are summer-only.

places.replacement_reason: Choose for a no-detour, low-cost spiritual-architecture morning when the aviation museum feels too institutional.
places.address: Great Auditorium, 21 Pilgrim Pathway, Ocean Grove, New Jersey

places.name: Lucy the Elephant
places.summary: A six-story building from 1881 shaped like an elephant. You climb a spiral staircase inside her body and come out in the little room on her back, looking at the sea.
places.why_go: You go inside a giant elephant and out onto her back. Silly on the surface, with a real story of people saving her from demolition.
places.best_fit_note: Primary fit: viki, stivka. The 65-step climb is optional; the surrounding grounds keep everyone included.

hours.note: Wednesday hours; tours every 45 minutes, subject to change.

places.address: Lucy the Elephant, 9200 Atlantic Avenue, Margate City, New Jersey
places.skip_strategy: The 65-step climb is optional; the surrounding grounds keep everyone included.

places.name: NAS Wildwood Aviation Museum
places.summary: A World War II naval air station museum inside a huge unheated wooden hangar. You can climb into cockpits and get close to engines and aircraft.
places.why_go: A real hangar, still cold and enormous, with aircraft you can touch. Completely different from a museum behind glass.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Gora's military and engineering interests and for Viki's big industrial images. The cold hangar is part of the experience.

hours.note: March-December daily hours; hangar is not climate controlled.

places.address: Naval Air Station Wildwood Aviation Museum, 500 Forrestal Road, Cape May, New Jersey

places.name: Cape May Victorian Architecture Walk
places.summary: A seaside district of highly decorated wooden houses with porches, towers and patterned shingles, lit at night by gas-style lamps. Very few American towns kept this many.
places.why_go: The whole town is the attraction. We walk and look instead of buying tickets for one house.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's photogenic streets and Stivka's interest in old churches and houses. Gora gets the social history behind the resort front.
places.address: Washington Street Mall, Cape May, New Jersey

hours.note: Confirm any interior access close to travel.

places.name: Cape May Spirits & Oddities Trolley
places.summary: A night trolley tour of ghost stories, Victorian superstitions, grave alarms, photographs of the dead and other strange old customs.
places.why_go: Folklore and dark local history after dark, and it keeps the evening social without turning into a club night.
places.best_fit_note: Primary fit: viki, stivka. Low physical demand; no skip path is required.

hours.note: Choose the actual October 7 departure when the date grid is released; do not substitute an unreviewed operator.

places.address: Ocean Street Trolley Stop, Cape May, New Jersey
places.skip_strategy: Low physical demand; no skip path is required.

places.name: Sunset Beach & SS Atlantus
places.summary: A free beach facing west, where the broken remains of a concrete ship from the First World War still sit just offshore. The sand holds polished quartz pebbles.
places.why_go: A concrete ship that sank where it stands, seen at sunset. Free, strange, and it works in almost any weather.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's sunset and shipwreck photo and for Gora's interest in things that failed. It gives everyone air before the ghost tour.

hours.note: State park gate is 8:00-20:00; the adjacent beach is visited only in daylight.

places.best_fit_note: Primary fit: viki, gora. Low physical demand; no skip path is required.

places.name: Fort Miles: Battery 519
places.summary: An underground World War II gun battery built to defend Delaware Bay, hidden under the dunes. It holds a 12-inch gun, mine-laying equipment and an outdoor artillery park.
places.why_go: A whole fort buried under a beautiful beach. You walk into the concrete and see what the dunes were really hiding.
places.best_fit_note: Primary fit: gora, stivka. Low physical demand; no skip path is required.

places.name: Great Dune & Fire-Control Tower
places.summary: A short climb over a moving sand dune to one of the concrete towers built to watch the sea for enemy ships.
places.why_go: Nature and war machinery in the same photograph, from one short walk.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's wide coast images and for Gora, who wants to see how the bay was watched and controlled.
places.address: Observation Tower, Fort Miles, Cape Henlopen State Park, Lewes, Delaware

hours.note: Confirm any interior access close to travel.

places.name: Berlin Main Street & Atlantic Hotel
places.summary: A well-preserved Eastern Shore town of brick shopfronts and porches, built around a Victorian hotel that has been part of local life for generations.
places.why_go: A deliberately quiet evening: walk, eat well, and let two days of ferries and forts settle.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's warm small-town feeling and for Stivka's low-key evening. Paco gets a calm reset before the longest coastal day.

hours.note: Confirm any interior access close to travel.

places.name: Zwaanendael Museum
places.summary: A small museum in a bright Dutch-style building, telling the story of Delaware's first European settlement and its difficult history at sea.
places.why_go: An odd little building that looks like it was lifted out of Holland, and an easier stop than the bunker if the ferry runs late.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's storybook building and for Gora's interest in settlement and shipwreck history. Stivka gets a small quiet museum.

places.summary: More than 7,500 objects inside a former poorhouse tell how whole communities lived on Virginia's barrier islands until storms and change emptied them.

places.best_fit_note: Good for Gora's love of forgotten history and for Viki's worn coastal objects. Stivka gets stories of community and survival.

places.summary: A Taiwanese pagoda and small garden beside the working Elizabeth River harbor, next to the old Freemason streets.

places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's architecture reflected in water and for Stivka's need for a quiet moment.

places.name: Edgar Cayce A.R.E. Headquarters
places.summary: The library and archive built around more than 14,000 trance readings by Edgar Cayce, on health, dreams, faith, Atlantis and psychic experience.
places.why_go: Believe it or not, it is a remarkable American mix of religion, medicine, business and outsider ideas, all kept in one archive.

places.best_fit_note: Built around Viki's memory photo. The others get coffee, public art and only a short dose of the tourist seafront.
places.address: King Neptune Statue, 3001 Atlantic Avenue, Virginia Beach, Virginia

places.name: Poe Museum & Enchanted Garden
places.summary: The oldest standing house in Richmond, holding Edgar Allan Poe's manuscripts and belongings, with a garden built around his poems. Two black cats, Edgar and Pluto, live there.

places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's gothic garden and cat photos, and for Gora's interest in the hard life behind famous writing. Stivka gets themes of death and conscience.

places.summary: An Arts-and-Crafts house on the water, filled with one family's very personal art collection, hand-carved interiors and gardens with sculpture.

places.best_fit_note: Primary fit: stivka. Low physical demand; no skip path is required.

places.name: B&O Railroad Museum
places.summary: The birthplace of American commercial railways, inside a huge round building from 1884. The locomotives run from horse-drawn beginnings to diesel engines.

places.best_fit_note: Good for Gora's love of machines and systems, and for Viki's circular iron and brick architecture. Paco gets a strong stop that works in any weather.

places.name: Baltimore Museum of Industry
places.summary: An 1865 oyster cannery on the water. Inside there are canning lines, a belt-driven machine shop and printing equipment, with the stories of the people who worked them.
places.why_go: Smaller than the railway museum, and on Sunday the staff actually run the machines instead of just labeling them.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Gora's interest in work and machinery, and for Viki's cannery textures and harbor views. Stivka gets human stories of craft and migration.

places.name: Mutter Museum

places.name: Metuchen Main Street Reset

hours.note: Confirm any interior access close to travel.
